commentBody: Well, I’m first here, so I guess that means it was another easy one.
I would like to say Mr. Sam E has been making fantastic Saturday minis, with spanners all around.

That took a few minutes and a bit of thought. Not a Saturday of old, but a fine Friday. A few too many expressions for my taste, but not too many proper nouns and a decent mix of interesting clues and surprising answers. Thank you, Brian.
Nice. Give me that little tingle a couple of times that I haven’t gotten to have in a while. Maybe, I wasn’t going to get it. Then… Bing, bang, boom! Thank you to the constructors.
What a great puzzle! Thanks bunches. Happy Saturday, y’all!

I enjoyed this puzzle, which I solved clockwise from the NE, finishing in the middle where I struggled for a bit.  I liked most of the fill, except for TEEHEEHEE. I liked the clue for RETINA, especially because the knee jerk answer, beauty, has the same number of letters.  WAVEHI slowed me down a little bit, as I tried wave to and wave at first.

I was surprised, and pleased, to see John HIATT, an old favorite of mine, especially his recordings with The Goners, who feature the great Louisiana guitarist, Sonny Landreth. HIATT has written some great songs, including Feels Like Rain, Slow Turning, and Memphis In The Meantime.

I also got a kick out HAGGIS, the bogeyman of all Scottish food jokes, making it into the puzzle.  Having spent a bit of time in Edinburgh over the past 12 months, the culinary scene there is both vibrant and sophisticated, and the days of deep fried everything are history.  HAGGIS, though,  is still part of the culture, and I actually rather like it.  But then again, I like scrapple too.
I was feeling good after doing so well on yesterday's puzzle. Not any more.
Is it just me or lots of teeheehee-ing recently?
Annoying. I couldn't solve the very tip of the SW corner. I thought WAVEHI was pretty awful. That said, the puzzle was OK but not terribly enjoyable.
*Said in the voice of the guy with the "Sickos" shirt from that Onion cartoon*: Yes . . . haha . . . YES!!!

Hmmm…I can’t say this was particularly difficult, but it was certainly the most lopsided solve I ever had. Maybe just because I got my first footholds on the right side, but literally I had the ENTIRE right side of the grid filled out with completely blank space on the left except for TEEH… and the incorrect IDOLS.

Sure, fool me on the Survivor clue of all things. I confess I apparently didn’t look at all the downs on the left because EAREXAM at least should have been a gimme.

Then I thought at first there was a lot of niche fill here—specifically sports and food—between the HAGGIS and PEARTARTS and WASABI and STEAMS and SINGES and SEARS on the one hand, and the TEBOWING and PELOTON (I only knew that as the name of the company) and NINERS and MIAmi on the other (I am so behind I still thought they were FLA). I felt like I was in the UberEats commercial with Matthew McConaughey suggesting that football was all a conspiracy to sell food. But maybe those just caught my eye, because ultimately there were a lot topics covered in this puzzle, 

Some interesting associations—TEEHEEHEE and HAHAS (which seemed a little light for a Saturday) and ELEVEN over NINErs.

So, pretty daring to have SLOG as an entry in a Saturday, but it certainly wasn’t for me, just a bit different. But ultimately at least an AVERAGE Saturday for these days so I’ll take it. And I learned more than a few things tonight and laughed at a few misdirects which is always my goal.

Even reading the description of HAGGIS (36D):

A savory pudding made from sheep's heart, liver, and lungs minced with oatmeal, onions, suet, and spices

makes me more than a bit nauseated.  Seems like the sort of dish one would try on a dare.

I really enjoyed this solve, felt like my hunches were connecting. THEBEEB, forexample.

Liked [It's in the eye of the beholder]/RETINA.

Lastly two of my favorite words are frangipane (almond cream, cited in one of this puzzle's clues) and frangipani (a type of flowering plant).

Said the Bartlett to the Bosc, "We make a good pear!"

(This pun appeals to a core audience.)

It's a good thing that I knew  "This side up container" (or a frag-ee-lee container) had to be CRATE....  Otherwise, I'm certain I would have clung to kiTTY for dear life. I guess it's also good thing I do know that other parts of the country use CATTY, so I accepted it and moved on. 

I believe I've only heard it in the wild once,
from a person I met from the deep south. Though I have also seen it on those little online quizzes you can do that try to predict where you're from based on how you answer your questions. Somehow they always think I'm either from Wisconsin, which I am, or Rhode island, which I'm definitely not. It's quite puzzling. Good thing I like puzzles!

Still, I'll forever be team kiTTY. 😏

Fun puzzle! I liked the clue for RETINA and was very happy that it wasn't beauty. Was surprised to see TEEHEEHEE again so soon, but I liked that it was crossed by HAHAS. 

Also really liked 14D's YOULIEDTOME for the work of fiction. Several others too! 

And nice not having to think at all about one down, and I do recommend, if you ever get around these parts, a trip to Duluth and North! Love that big old Lake Superior!!

Tonight my friend and I had dinner out and it was going to be between sushi and Chinese, so 1A and 2A really spoke to me. Ultimately, it was decided because, though not shumai, and though I love wasabi, we'd go with Szechuan because I wanted soup dumplings. 

To sum up, they WEREGOOD! Har!

Thanks, Brian, for the J. HIATT reference. John HIATT’s songbook is extensive and impressive. If you want to check out something recent, his 2021 album with the Jerry Douglas Band, Leftover Feelings, is excellent. A sample: https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=zEBVevAr1cQ

Took me a bit longer than Saturdays of late, so I appreciated the challenge. Was it the puzzle or the pain meds I’m on from a wee procedure yesterday—I’ll never know. 

My husband says CATTY corner, I say kitty corner, yet we were born not quite 500 miles apart. Which, as I tell my current European colleagues, is just a pleasant weekend drive.

I struggled a lot with this one.  

I was just bedeviled by topics that I have no familiarity with at all, like bike racing, pines with nuts (which made my beat my head repeatedly when I got NUTPINE), pear tarts with their frangipane goop, the culinary arts, gymnasts, webisodes, Madden games with TEBOWING, shopping sprees, , talons on kites ( 😱??? Or is there a raptor called a "kite")

Just one nightmare after another.

I mean right off the bat [Prepares, as shumai], I assume that's food, but I have no idea what kind.  My suspicion is that it's one of the synthetic foods from Cronenberg's, "eXistenZ".

Just flat out brutal.  Torturous.  Like fingernail-pulling.

But worst of all...completely fair.  Mr.  Calahan just threw pitch after pitch that I could not hit.

So I finally gave up, put in my best guesses, hit the Reveal Puzzle.  I had one typo, and errors in four connected squares, the first two letters of HAUL and CATTY.  Worst outing in a long time.

That part of the puzzle was especially hard for me.  Every single guess I had was equally reasonable, and they all eliminated each other with crosses.

Gladium depono.

Been dog's years since a Saturday took me an hour.

Thanks, Brian, for the walk down pre-easening lane.

DEADHEADING and WEBISODES was a natick until the memory-palace fog slowly burned off to reveal both.
Lost several minutes to my conviction that [Watch party?] would be STAKEOUT
Lovely!

Friday was difficult for me, but today was oddly easy. Maybe because a lot of the fill seems well suited for someone who grew up eating STEAMed shumai and rooting for the NINERS in the Bay Area and of an age to remember when Tim TEBOW was a thing, TEEHEEHEE.
no offense Brian and Will -  you wave to someone or say hi - you don't 'wave hi' -  Aloha! and Namaste for a truly nerdy Saturday puzzle.

I must be old.  (Silence, Andrzej!)

Early conversating about KITTY vs CATTY entirely ignores what I clung to in the face of ever-mounting crossing evidence:  the original CATER.

I'm KITTY-corner though my southern relations are CATTY-corner so I got that, but some of the rest was a SLOG for me.    Was entertained by the  puzzling obfuscating cluing, though many expressions were foreign to me with few crossings to help.    
I believe I prefer HAGGIS to Survivor though they both have unappealing components.

From the two people divided by a common language department:  Pudding here usually means dessert. What most of you call pudding we call custard. Pudding here can also mean something savoury like Yorkshire pudding, black pudding (essential for a “full English” breakfast), white pudding and haggis, which some of us find quite tasty especially with a wee dram.  The word pudding originally meant offal and Pudding Lane in London was where carts carrying offal traveled to the Thames to dump their bloody loads.  It’s also where the Great Fire of London started in 1666 and one of the world’s first one-way streets.

WAVE HI... That was a stain on an otherwise very well clued and challenging puzzle. It took me something like 20 minutes to let go of my conviction that it absolutely had to be WAVE at or WAVE to.

It took extra long time, but I was able to solve the puzzle on my own, pretty much. I just checked online if my guess of the QB move was correct: crosses and memories of the brief period when my wife watched American football some years ago had given me TEBOWI__, and I thought the entry might be TEBOWING, but it looked so strange I felt I needed to confirm if it was right (btw, while Polish athletes often cross themselves before competing, the sort of religious spectacle Tebow used to make of himself looked positively medieval to me).

I'm hopeless with bird names in English but somehow I remembered a kite was a bird, which made the SW corner solveable for me - I found it the hardest section of the puzzle, nearly impossible to deal with, and every little bit helped.

As someone who prefers actual words as crossword entries, I wasn't particularly happy with TEEHEEHEE crossing HAHAS, but over the years I have accepted it's the sort of thing that NYT puzzles will occasionally feature (the Polish giggle is different, btw; we say "hi hi", or "hee hee" to you. No "tee" in sight).

What's a CATTY-corner? Of course it's mentioned but not explained in the column... (Again: why have a tricky clues section if you're not gonna, you know, actually elaborate on tricky clues and answers there?)
I thought it was CADDY corner, which is what I've always heard. :/

MEAN is truly a good title for this puzzle - Tebow himself is part of this operation: Ironic this puzzle came out the day this came out: https://apnews.com/article/tim-tebow-life-surge-4dbc0ed030c48ab3bf7516b76cb5f14a

I’m trying to think when the BBC (Aunty Beeb) had a coat of arms as its logo, and I can’t picture one at all. They were circular until the ‘30s, and since then have been a variation of the letters in individual boxes.

Rose: TEEHEEHEE
Thorn: TEBOWING

I award 3/5 Grant R stars

Thanks for the puzzle Brian C
This one got the better of me. Not familiar with US directions and timezones, so those threw me. Had to reveal in the SW corner... Ironically. Wonder if that was on purpose?

Am I the only one that didn't understand HHH = ETAS? We are so conditioned to seeing ETA as Estimated Time of Arrival. I had to get some help to realize not for me to give a Delta epsilon Zeta data it was the Greek letter eta. (And I know the Greek alphabet!)

I wasn't that keen on this one. Rather a lot of general knowledge I just didn't know, although I liked RETINA. 

Red KITES were almost extinct, but have been reintroduced to the UK, which now has 15% of the global population.

I Loved [HHH] for ETAS.  I see that it's been used before, but it was still a surprise.  My first thought was veep, but crosses prohibited that.

[Real page-turner] for SPEED READER  was another favorite.

Sports clues used to really stump me.  Filling in NINERS with just the N, MIA with no crosses, and TEBOWING with just the TE showed me how far I've come.  I still know next to nothing about the games, but I can fake it enough for crosswords.

Nice puzzle with some areas of friction.  I would have liked a little more of that, but here we are.

Agree with Tough SW corner. Aha, kite the bird. That’s why I couldn't fit tail into a 5 letter spot. I also wanted idols in the Surviver spot but that didn't last long.  By the way, I am happy to silently 'wave hi' to anyone I meet when I'm listening to music or a podcast with my ear buds in so let's 'get a grip' there on 35D!

Hmmm …. A three-stack crossing a five-stack.  Try making one of those, or better yet, try making one of those and keeping the grid sans junk.

I saw a video a few days ago of a six-year-old who solved a Rubik’s cube five times in a row, averaging 4.52 seconds per solve, for a female world record.  Creating a grid like today’s is maybe not that, but it’s not far away.

So high props to Brian for coming up with this answer set.  

And high props as well for the cluing.  My five favorite clues, it turns out, are all original.  [A bit corrupt, perhaps?] for DATA ROT – Hah!  And what a way to class up RETINA with [It’s in the eye of the beholder]!

Add seven NYT answer debuts for freshness, including the terrific WE’RE GOOD, and much brain-loving resistance, and this was rich with happy-pings for me, Brian.  Thank you, sir!
Does anyone else have a problem with the puzzle jumping up after entering ? It resets where the page is but doesn't move the cursor. I've been to the bot but that wasn't helpful.

A tip of the cap to ya!

Fair fa' your honest, sleekit grid 
Great chieftain o' the puddin-clue!
Aboon them a' ye tak me starn,
Painch, tripe, or oreos:
Weel are ye wordy o' a good skin
As lang's my arm.
Good challenging puzzle overall but I find the frequent TEEHEE entries a little banal and childish so to have HAHA in addition sorta ruined it for me… grow up maybe?

Deadheading refers to airline crew that are not working the flight but are traveling to the destination to work a different flight.  Flying for free as an airline employee is known as nonrevving (no revenue) or going standby.
All airline employees can non-rev, but only flight crew are allowed to deadhead.

Found this one a bit easier than yesterday's; solved without assistance in just under 30 minutes. I suppose I learned several new terms from this puzzle, but didn't find it all that interesting or enjoyable.

This puzzle was not made with me in mind. The middle did me in: PEARTARTS and TEBOWING and PELOTON, WEBISODES, TRADE DEAL AND TEEHEEHEE (again). I knew instantly that kite would be the bird, but couldn't come up with TALON. For some strange reason, DEADHEADING was a gimme, and I should have gotten SPEED READER, but I guess I was too forlorn at that point to give it a little more time. 

I don't like to give up, but this time I had no choice. Oh, well, you can't win 'em all.
What a relief that the unwanted cursor feature when solving on computers has disappeared!

There were a couple of rather tart crossing pairs for which I had to just hope they would reassure me of their okayness upon completion.

Fringybangs was new to me.
Good puzzly puzzle!

I can live with including both ALI and ALY.  I’m not thrilled with having both SEARS and SINGES, but it’s not a big deal.  But, in my humble opinion,  having both HAHAS and TEEHEEHEE should have been enough for the editors to send the puzzle back for improvement.

Wow.
I haven’t prepared anything,
but I’d like to thank the Academy of Stubborness,

the NE corner,
the SE corner,
the SW corner,
and most of all-

the NE corner for getting me
to where I am,
and for believing in me as
I stared blankly at the center abyss.

You never gave up on me and, well,

I owe it all to you.

Dad, this one’s for you.

Thank you all so much.

I made this harder on myself than I had to, but in an interesting way.

For 35a (Online show pieces) I had WEBIS__ES, but somehow not noticing that “I”, I filled in WEB[I]SitES - thinking I had put in “websites” and that the clue was just not great…

This lead to having _EA_HEAtING for 17d (Riding free as an employee in airline lingo). I filled in sEAtHEAtING, which honestly sounded like a great and correct answer (way better than “deadheading” which I got to eventually). Took a while to correct that area.

What I learned: Deadheading (in airline lingo) specifically refers to free on-the-clock travel with the airline transporting you to your next assignment. Free personal travel (when there is a seat available) is called non-revenue travel or “non-revving” for short 🤓

Yowzers. This was my slumdog bankruptcy puzzle. Very tough for me, but a fair puzzle. I didn't even get TEBOWING as I had TUSHPUSH instead because I'd fallen for the BEAUTY trap vs RETINA. Yeesh. Cheers!
Really good stuff!
Am I the only one who is neither team kitty nor team catty? No idea what either of them are...!
This took me waaay over my average. That makes me very happy. Great job Brian!
1D was diabolical! Like everyone else I had NNE, assuming they were talking about the Duluth and Minneapolis in Jordan.
Made me work!

I had no idea and convinced myself of AVer, PELeTON, and TEBOrING.  I watch bike racing and I somehow squished on PELOTON.

Never have I ever seen or used a capital eta before.  Kept wondering how to fit something about Hubert Humphrey in.  Did finally get through the crosses.   I use small eta frequently!

Goodness that was a toughie. But I liked it, the obligatory sports/name refs notwithstanding.
Call me team kitty corner, not to be confused with hospital corners; the old fashioned method of tucking in a flat sheet. Woe betide the nurse (often moi) who did a sloppy job on those. Matron would SEAR you with a look. 

I knew 7A but not 1A, which held up that corner a bit. I had no idea the BBC had a coat of arms, I had to google it. Nation Shall Speak Peace Unto Nation. Hmmm, who could do with adopting that motto?

Re DEADHEADING. I saw an earlier comment confirming what I thought (checked with the resident pilot). That does only apply to positioning air crew. It’s Standby for every other employee.

Very tough, thoroughly absorbing, and very gratifying when I finally solved it without a single cheat.

Can there be anything more maddening than (I thought) having an answer on the tip of my tongue and not being able to access it?  I watched maybe 3 seasons of "The Survivor" until the shtick and sameness drove me away.  And I couldn't for the life of me remember the highly prized rewards.  They had to begin with a T because of TALON, but what were they???  TORCH?  I need a 5-letter plural.   Well into the puzzle, I finally remember that the biggest prize conferred IMMUNITY -- but IMMUNITY is much too long.  Wasn't it an IDOL?  Oh, to have a halfway decent memory.

Finally, finally -- and only after I change WAVE TO to WAVE HI and AVER to AVOW -- do I get TARPS.  Hey, everyone, IT'S NOT MY FAULT!!!!!  I'm pretty sure during the seasons I watched, TARPS had yet to be given out to any of the Survivors. The writers must have come up with the idea later in the run.  I'd bet the bank on it!

Aha -- it's TEBOWING -- named after the quarterback.  I thought there was a TBONE formation in football that was maybe now being spelled TEBONE -- but neither AVER nor AVOW would give me the needed N.

Most of my "suffering" was in the SW -- although SENTRIES before SENTINEL caused me some headaches on the East Coast.

All the difficulty was in the clues rather than in arcane bits of trivia.  Meaning WE'RE GOOD, Brian and I loved this!

Tough one for me and couldn't quite work it all out. More than a couple of completely unfamiliar answers (WEBISODES, DATAROT for example). No big deal. And my usual puzzle find. A Thursday from August 26, 2021 by Ashish Vengsarkar. Don't recall another one like this. Some examples with the crossing letter in parentheses. MAL(I) SUR(I)NAME (those clued as MAL and SURNAME NO(R)WAY (R)WANDA (NOWAY and WANDA) TONG(A) PANAM(A) And there were others. And then, the 'reveal': CROSSCOUNTRY Thought that was pretty clever. Here's the link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=8/26/2021&h=57a ....
So satisfying! Just challenging enough.

Tough but fair, took me 30% longer than my Saturday average. Today I learned about both TEBOWING and DEADHEADING. Got stuck on SENTRIES for the longest time, a 'party' being either a person or a group. 
And with no idea what frangipane is, I had TIRAMISUS clogging up the middle of the board. Seems I was thinking of mascarpone, haha teeheehee. 
Challenging, but in no way a slog. Well done!

90% of this puzzle felt like a standard 2026 Saturday…and then there was WAVEHI.

Along with many others, it took me so long to get past my instant conviction that this silent greeting would involve waving “at” or “to” the other person. That blocked me from seeing PHONED or SINGES, which in turn kept me from getting TARPS (having never watched a single episode of Survivor, I didn’t really even try to get that one without the crosses).

Great little corner!

I guess I was on the same wavelength as the constructor, because most of my temporary answers worked out. Even WAVE HI seemed reasonable to me. I really liked the RETINA clue and enjoyed the puzzle overall. Didn’t know DATA ROT - does that refer to a specific process, or just any old corruption?
"retina" was diabolical! Of course I thought it was BEAUTY at first, but then I had PATINA for the longest time.
TEEHEEHEEs in the rear view mirror _feel_ more recent than they appear…

40 Across: the clue was “Assert” while the answer was AVOW.

Avow - declare openly, confess, or acknowledge frankly, often taking personal responsibility for the statement or belief. 

Aver - To affirm, assert, or declare positively and formally that something is true. 

What am I missing?

Pecans and Pumpkins and PEAR TARTs, Oh My. What is this, pie day? Okay by me. After my initial hands thrown up in the air, this is impossible response, it went rather smoothly, so I am a happy camper. (Unlike for many, my problem wasn't HI, it was WAVE.) I first came across John HIATT, because of a Bonnie Raitt cover decades ago. And here she is With a Thing Called Love. https://youtu.be/rK1HC8weDlM?si=cggCjmTB9HCColPp

I have to tell ya—I did not expect to find this so distinctly unenjoyable.

Not here to rain on parades; here to speak for those too afraid now. ;)

Fun personal fact; this actually happened to me:       The very first NYT full crossword I did, I got every single word. It still sits there, my streak of one. I entertain the idea that it was a brand-newbie algorithm thing. It was a big deal. And that I did so once, in a Sunday, has me satisfied for life.
Tougher than the average (meaner than the mean)
Brutal. Bravo!

No complaints here!  Kind of a perfect Saturday (yes, for me, folks).  Chewy, tough, but also not back breaking.  (XWStats users voted "Hard".)  I had an awful lot of blank space in the middle for a long time.  Everything was ultimately fair and solvable.

I had Idols for Survivor and FLA for Marlins for too long.  You Lied and Side Bangs were unexpectedly hard and I had "free trade" stuck for a while.  And of course I had the wrong kite in mind.

Really fine construction on this.  Bravo.  More Saturday Saturdays please!
Worked and worked!  I loved this.  I won't say the clues MISdirected, but they INdirected over and over and I enjoyed it enormously!
Tough. Very tough.

This was definitely not a run-of-the-mill across-down-across-done solve. First time through the Acrosses I had 8 guesses, only six of which survived. So, slow solve.

But nay. Was almost done a full 10 minutes ahead of my recent average (as computed by xwstats) and a full 20 minutes ahead of my long term average (as computed by NYT), lacking only the "rang" and "toast" entries. So, fast solve.

But nay! A lot of possibilities there. And TARPS, which sounded imminently logical (I refuse to watch that show) wouldn't go with either WAVEat or WAVEto. 

Dithered around awhile before pulling out several answers I was confident of. Saw that WAVEHI solved all my problems. Finished in average time. 

Felt kind of like driving east on I-90 at about 10 AM.
Not enjoyable

Three more thoughts:

Team "Catty Corner" here.

With "STEM field concern" I feel heard, but not enough. 

"Exclave's spot" was my favorite clue. I'd never heard of "exclave" but instantly knew what it must be and what the answer must be. What a fun way to learn a new word.

I haven’t even started today’s big puzzle yet bc I was busy finishing Thursday’s. It was the Scrabble themed one, and I just want to tell Jeff Stillman how much fun it was (though he might not see this) 
It took me quite a while to see the theme and understand how there could be any fill that was only 2 letters. Can’t say it was a FAST solve but it was definitely a fun solve and it brought me a joy-filled challenge on a very difficult day. Thanks Jeff 😊😊

I thought I recognized the shape, I've enjoyed the previous puzzles on this grid. And this was no different - I thought it was going to be too tough based on how few words I got on my first pass, but I was able to gradually work my way back through it and finish it without taking a break. Pretty much my ideal "tough but doable" Saturday solve.
The 🔍 feature inside the comments is v handy, today I needed it for an HHH explanation.
Hi - Brian - Loved your puzzle! Hope everyone in the Northeast is safe from/in the storm. I'm visiting my family in TN, and worried about my house in CT. Have a good Saturday.
Wow! Great puzzle. Haha. Heehee.

Ah yes, one of those puzzles that would have been enjoyable if not for the streak.  The streak turns it into googling things and checking the answer key so you don't have to be mocked by the puzzle about how you totally *had* a streak and now it's gone, and you have to be reminded of that every single day moving forward.  Without it I'd ask for some help and then happily just solve from letter crossings -- you know, like a real puzzle.  Once again I cannot overstate how much gamification can ruin enjoyment for some folks, even while many many people find it a more engaging element.  (If I *could* turn it off, I *would*, for all of you preparing to comment about it.)
Enjoyed...peloton threw me - only knew it as a name for equipment. Learned something new...
Loved the crossed laughs and the fun misdirects. Fast solve for a Saturday but very fun!

Ooooo! I did the thing where I got stuck so I went and took a shower and did the dishes, then came back and started seeing things! That totally works.
Also, does anyone else besides me have trouble sometimes "seeing" the down answers? When that happens I type out what I have with underlines for spaces and often I'll suddenly see what should go there. Works at least half the time.

I very much enjoyed this puzzle — lots of clever clueing and some fun entries like YOU LIED TO ME, SIDE BANGS (that's a thing?), DATA ROT, NUT PINE (both new to me). 

Here's the thing about CATTY-corner: I wondered about the spelling, and it turns out that Merriam-Webster gives *three* different spellings for this word! kitty-corner is the preferred spelling, with both catty-corner and catercorner designated by "or less commonly" ... which is M-W's *middle level* of spelling variants beyond the preferred spelling, separated by "or" or "or less commonly" or "also" — in that order. I'm surprised how many different spelling and pronunciations are all considered to be the same word.

As seems usual lately, the Friday puzzle solved like a Saturday puzzle and the Saturday solved like a Friday. Is this switcheroo real or a hallucination? If real, is it random fluctuation or intentional? I wonder if the editors would consider communicating with crossword fans about this, maybe through the comments here.
Needed a dictionary's help with "anthropopithecus" but I now know a new word!

I keep thanking Deb for telling readers of Wordplay to try the Friday and Saturday puzzles.  I don't always succeed without Google, but this weekend was special and I did both with not lookups.  It feels so good.  And to make the days evens better, we are having two perfect fall days in Pittsburgh.  (I moved here from NY about 9 years ago but haven't bothered to update my location.)
Great puzzle!!!! Starting to really love saturdays!

I really thought I'd have to give in and look things up, but I kept coming back to it and making little bits of headway and I got it! This is definitely the hardest puzzle I've ever solved with no lookups. It was a lot of fun! Great wordplay. I do disagree with catty corner, though :)
“Well rounded” was a little bit gross, my dude.
There's only one true answer to "result of shopping spree": BILL.

This was a very difficult puzzle!  My coffee got cold...and then there was all the erasing!  (I had a list of alternative entries in the margin, which habit came in very handy.)  
PhysicsDaughter is here; she and DHubby have a line-up of college football games to monitor--Penn State being the most important; I heard them discussing how to use various devices so they could watch more than one game at a time.  Ye gods.  
I will be sequestered in a room, sewing, until it's time for me to make dinner.  DHubby managed to upend a glass of water at the dinner table--claiming it was "just a dribble"--so I'll just note that the D can stand for more than "Dear."  But then he made an "emergency" trip to get an ingredient I needed for a recipe, so redemption IS possible.

I hope we see more Saturday puzzles of this caliber.

Should not give Tebow any more seconds of fame than he's already had. Otherwise a tricky and good puzzle. 

Had TIARA for the longest time so got stuck in the SW Corner for a bit. Also couldn't figure out what we were waving (AT/TO/HI)! Still a decent time for me.
hated it. thanks
